notes: §1985:VI.5.14.2 prints the clause as an optional USAGE IS (IS not underlined) and one of BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL, COMP, DISPLAY, INDEX and PACKED-DECIMAL. The grammar rule usageClause is that shape (IS only after USAGE, exactly one usageKeyword) and PictureAnalyzer.ParseUsage resolves the six words, COMP as COMPUTATIONAL. usageKeyword is a superset, and 1985 refuses the rest by name: VersionConformancePass.GateDataItem asks UsageConstructId of every bound item, which answers COBOL0900 below 2002, 2014 or 2023 for NATIONAL, BIT, POINTER, PROGRAM-POINTER, FUNCTION-POINTER, OBJECT REFERENCE, MESSAGE-TAG, the BINARY-CHAR family and the FLOAT usages; VisitUsageClause refuses WITH NO SIGN and the float format phrases; DataBinder.ScreenUsagePhrases refuses SIGNED or UNSIGNED on BINARY (COBOL4733); ClosedFormatPass.ScreenClauseRepetition refuses a second USAGE clause in one entry (COBOL2423). COMP-1 to COMP-5 and COMPUTATIONAL-1 to -5 are accepted at 85 as documented nonstandard extensions (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.2) that ParseUsage flags under --flag-extensions (COBOL2894), which §1985:I.1.5.2.5.2 admits: "A conforming implementation of Standard COBOL must provide a warning mechanism, which optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate, if appropriate, that a program contains nonstandard extensions that are included in the implementation." The witness declares the six usages with and without USAGE and IS and computes with them. Probed further at --std 85 (37 entries): the six in every spelling, lower case, and a group USAGE repeated on a subordinate item are accepted; IS without USAGE, USAGE or USAGE IS with no word, USAGE ARE, two usages in one entry, COMPUTATION, PACKED, DISPLAY-1, BINARY SIGNED, BINARY HIGH-ORDER-LEFT and each later-edition usage are refused; COMP-3 and COMP-1 compile and draw COBOL2894 with --flag-extensions.

next.reason: 1985: "[USAGE IS] {BINARY|COMPUTATIONAL|COMP|DISPLAY|INDEX|PACKED-DECIMAL}"; 2023: "BINARY-CHAR ... BIT ... FLOAT-BINARY-32 ... NATIONAL ... PACKED-DECIMAL [ WITH NO SIGN ] ... POINTER". The 2023 format keeps all six 1985 usages but adds alternatives (BIT, NATIONAL, FLOAT-*, POINTER, etc.) and WITH NO SIGN, so programs refused in 1985 are now accepted.
